goal_scope: CIFAR100/TinyImageNet common forward exact-ReLU HybridZ path

algorithm.stable_active: Represent y=x by the existing preactivation affine expression instead of a fresh box factor plus equality band.
algorithm.unstable: Retain the existing local output factor, one binary phase factor, and all three exact Big-M facets.
algorithm.affine_execution: Forward-only sparse composition; no backward pass, dual, sampled input, or solver.

fixed_independent_cube_control.purpose: Separate stable-active relation deletion from the additional phase stabilization caused by tighter correlated forward expressions.
fixed_independent_cube_control.interpretation: The phase-preserving structural case is still material in rows/factors, but only a DAG that avoids flat intermediates can make it a viable common path.

existing_survivor_prescreen_with_old_cha.decision: Fast, but old chain cuts restore most rows and violate the intended no-materialization DAG representation.

profile.diagnosis: Full intermediate residual tensors, not exact-ReLU row construction, dominate latency.

tinyimagenet_medium_iid17.skip_reason: The smaller CIFAR100 candidate failed the mandatory frontend performance gate and the GPU feasibility path consumed excessive memory.

decision: Do not integrate the flat CPU or GPU candidate and do not run a solver or TinyImageNet. The fixed-independent-cube control still deletes 79.5 percent of source rows without changing the 1,052 phase classifications, but its flat build is 0.265x. The material structural reduction justifies only a future single forward DAG implementation which never expands the 7M-20M-nnz residual intermediates; it must first beat the retained build by at least 1.5x on the same topology.
